title: Teaching Technological Education in the Intermediate-Senior Divisions - A
description: This course begins to prepare students to be qualified teachers of Technological Education in Ontario classrooms. It allows students to examine the theories, philosophies, knowledge, policies and practices specific to teaching Technological Education in the intermediate and senior grades. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (BEd) degree program.

title: Teaching Technological Education in the Intermediate-Senior Division - B
description: This course continues to prepare students to be qualified teachers of Technological Education in Ontario classrooms. It develops students' expertise in the theories, philosophies, knowledge, policies and practices specific to teaching Technological Education areas in order to further develop students' expertise for teaching this subject. ED/TECH 4000 (Part A) is a prerequisite for this course. Only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (BEd) program.

title: Curriculum Connections for Technological Education
description: This course examines cross-curricular connections for the teaching and learning of technological education in Ontario schools. It explores cross-curricular approaches to teaching technological education, and its curricular connections to literacy, numeracy, STEM, experiential education, environmental/sustainability education, and social justice. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (Technological Education) program.

title: Teaching Design Thinking Within Technology Frameworks
description: Activating design thinking theories, techniques, and mindsets, this course examines a range of problem-solving methods and design processes integral to all broad-based technologies in the Ontario technological education curriculum. Students will be introduced to practical, process-focused frameworks for developing student projects in the intermediate/senior classroom. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (Technological Education) program.

title: Disruptive Technology Innovation & Entrepreneurship
description: Technology can create, reshape and destroy whole industries. AirBnB, UBER, digital cameras and cell phones are some recent examples. This course introduces concepts of how technology can create opportunities leading to new industries or disruption of existing industries. Topics to be introduced include 3D printing, drones, robotics/automation, sensors, AI and big data, genomic sequencing, nanotech/advanced materials, microfluidics/microfabrication, energy storage/renewable energy/sustainability, blockchain and the internet of things. These topics are made accessible to students of non-technical disciplines. Insights gained into tech disruption will be encapsulated within concepts of entrepreneurship to empower students to distinguish between technology hype vs reality and assist in forecasting future high-impact industry sectors.

title: Leadership and Teamwork I
description: Each year of the Mechatronics program has a required Leadership and Teamwork component. This course is the mechanism used to manage that course requirement.

title: Mechatronics Work-Term I
description: This course is specifically designed for Mechatronics Engineering students to enrol during their work term. In addition to the work, students reflect on the relationship of their academic learning to the work experience. Employers also provide their evaluation of the student's performance. Successful completion of at least two work term courses is a requirement of the Mechatronics Engineering program. Prerequisites: Open only to students with good standing in the Mechatronics Engineering program. This is normally satisfied by completing 45 credits from the TRON degree program checklist including TRON2000 and being in good standing in the TRON program.

title: Leadership and Teamwork II
description: Each year of the Mechatronics program has a required Leadership and Teamwork component. This course is the mechanism used to manage that course requirement.

title: Legal Values: Commercializing IP
description: Navigating legal issues is crucial to the commercialization of new technologies. This course will examine the application of substantive intellectual property (IP) law in the context of IP management for in-house lawyers or IP managers within IP-rich organizations. Through case studies and facilitated discussion, students will apply principles central to IP management, including creation, development, protection, and exploitation of intellectual property rights as a business asset. Guest speakers will supplement the course's examination of key technology specific issues relating to high technology and sciences. In particular, this course will examine the process of creating, capturing, protecting, leveraging and transferring technology and ideas, including internal strategies designed to create a culture of innovation; deciding whether, what, where, and how to obtain IP registrations and the related economics; the development of a commercialization strategy (such as selecting the target market and application for the idea) and business model; drafting and negotiating related agreements; offensive and defensive IP strategies; assessing competitive IP; negotiating and interpreting IP sensitive contracts; and transactional IP processes. Course Credit Exclusion: LW-LAW 3591M 3.00

title: Leadership and Teamwork III
description: Each year of the Mechatronics program has a required Leadership and Teamwork component. This course is the mechanism used to manage that course requirement.

title: Management of Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Cross-Campus Capstone Classroom (C4) Management is a high impact finishing program for C4 alumni. Students are given the opportunity to lead teams created from a group of undergraduates who are registered in C4 Launchpad and Primer. Together they will work intensively over a semester on one large, complex multi-disciplinary project, pitched by a single partner. Prerequisite: LE/ENG 2400 3.00 or LE/ENG 3400 3.00 or LE/ENG 4401 6.00 or LE/ENG 4402 6.00.

title: Leadership and Teamwork IV
description: Each year of the Mechatronics program has a required Leadership and Teamwork component. This course is the mechanism used to manage that course requirement.

title: Methodology of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description: This course introduces principles and practices of English language teaching, including communicative language teaching, planning, assessment, instructional techniques, and the appropriate use of resources. The course helps students develop a critical, reflective teaching practice that includes the skills to design and deliver an effective, learner-centered program in a range of contexts. NOTE: This blended course includes both online and in-class instruction. Course credit exclusion: ED/TESL 3200 6.00

title: Practicum in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description: The course provides an experiential education opportunity to put theory into practice, integrating blended online and in-class instruction alongside placement at a variety of English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction settings. Students complete 50 practicum hours (30 hours observation and 20 hours practice teaching). Note: This course may be taken concurrently with, but not before AP/TESL 3200 6.00. Course credit exclusion: ED/TESL 3300 6.00.

title: Socio-Political Issues in Second Language Teaching
description: Teaching English to speakers of other languages (TESOL) takes place within a complex socio-political context. Selected issues are used to consider how this context influences the teaching/learning process. NOTE: This blended course includes both online and in-class instruction. CCE: AP/LING 3600 3.00

title: Introduction to Acting I
description: Introduces the principles, processes and skills of acting for the stage. Students will rehearse and perform a variety of class presentations, and actively participate in warm-ups, theatre games and acting exercises. A practical studio course with a strong written component to the curriculum. Required of all first-year theatre majors. Open only to theatre majors. Corequisites: FA/THEA 1100 3.00 and FA/THEA 1200 6.00. Note: A minimum of two rehearsal hours per week may be required.

title: Introduction to Acting II
description: Continues the exploration of the principles, processes and skills of acting for the stage commenced in FA/THEA 1010 3.00, with a particular emphasis on basic script analysis and the rehearsing and performing of monologues and scenes. A practical studio course with is a strong written component to the curriculum. Open to theatre majors only. Pre-requisite: a minimum grade of 'C+' in FA/THEA 1010 3.00, and/or permission of the department.

title: Introduction to Stagecraft I
description: Introduces the fundamentals and vocabulary of design, lighting and stagecraft (in any given year this could include sound, props, paint etc.). Corequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1200 6.00. Course credit exclusion: FA/THEA 1100 6.00, FA/DANC 1270 3.00. Note: Open to theatre majors only or permission of the department. Note: Evening and/or weekend crew work on department productions is required, as well as lab hours.

title: Introduction to Production Practicum
description: This is a new course to make production practicum (The Experiential Education cornerstone of the BFA in Production/Design) available to first year students who are accepted to the Theatre Department with a production portfolio and a stated intent to join the BFA in Production/Design or who demonstrate aptitude though their fall term crew assignments in Stage Craft 1. This will allow Production Practicum to be offered to all years of theatre educa-tion in the Department. Production Practicum courses allow students to work on professionally modelled theatre productions with professional directors, Faculty, designers, choreographers, and technical staff. Students experience hands-on, practical, dynamic theatre challenges in these student-led productions guided by professional mentors and advisors. This is a practical course in theatre production. The experiential learning in this course focuses on advanced skills in theatre production and technical work scaled to the student's year of study and experience. As expected with the mounting of a full-scale piece of theatre, a significant time commitment is associated with Production Practicum courses beyond weekly class meetings, including standard crew hours and meetings. Prerequisites: by permission of the Production/Design Area. Co-requisite: At least one other studio course in theatre production. By permission only. By permission of the Department.

title: Introduction to Stagecraft II
description: Continues the introduction to the basics of theatrical production begun in FA/THEA 1100 3.00. Previously offered as: FA/THEA 1100 6.00. Note: Open to theatre majors only or permission of the department.

title: Introduction to Theatre and Performance
description: Designed to introduce Theatre students to the key concepts and debates animating Theatre Studies today. Beginning with the overarching question ""What is theatre and why/how do we study it?"" students will explore a wide range of topics, including (but not limited to) audience, space, time, bodies, community, spectacle, history, and politics. The course will also introduce students to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches for studying theatre and performance, e.g. performance ethnography, theatre historiography, community activism, practice-based research, educational outreach. Students will have opportunities to work individually as well as collaboratively on written and performance projects. They will also become familiar with Toronto's lively theatre and performance ecology through visits to a wide range of performances over the course of the year. Corequisite: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00.

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides an introductory practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre. Prerequisite: By permission of the department.

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides an introductory practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre. Prerequisite: By permission of the department.

title: Voice: Breath, Sound, Text
description: Introduces the rudiments of voice training for the actor with an exploration of breath awareness, vocal sounding, and the personalization of imagistic poetry; introduces basic vocal anatomy and physiology; and begins an investigation of storytelling for the actor. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00, FA/THEA 1200 6.00. Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 1011 3.00 and/or audition plus permission of the department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 2020 3.00, FA/THEA 2030 3.00. Open to theatre majors only.

title: Acting & Devising
description: Introduces acting techniques through group and individual character building, with a focus on situational devised and improvisational storytelling. There is a strong emphasis on combining voice, movement and thought, through embodiment. Script analysis and research methods are explored. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1011 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00, FA/THEA 1200 6.00 and/or audition plus permission of the department. Grade of B or better in THEA 1011 3.00 or permission of the department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 2010 3.00 and FA/THEA 2020 3.00. Open to majors only.

title: Acting: Scene Study
description: Furthers script analysis using previously published plays that challenge and strengthen the students' learning path. Emphasis is placed more upon character objectives, managing character emotions, and continuing the student's overall embodiment while applying tactics to any given character role. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2020 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to theatre majors only.

title: Movement: Breath, Strength, Ease
description: An introduction to foundational movement techniques necessary for the physical actor. This course will investigate the integrated connection of movement to breath, while building strength and physical organization. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1011 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 and FA/THEA 1200 6.00 and/or audition plus permission of the department. Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 1011 3.00 or permission of the department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 2010 3.00 and FA/THEA 2020 3.00. Open to majors only.

title: Introduction to Devised Theatre
description: Offers students an introduction to the devising of theatre in all aspects, from conception to execution. Classroom exercises and performance project assignments will allow students to explore the processes and skills of the theatre practitioner. Practical studio course. Prerequisite: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2020 3.00, FA/THEA 2050 3.00, or FA/THEA 2141 3.00, or permission of the department. Open to theatre majors only. Note: Plus rehearsal hours.

title: Voice and Speech I
description: An introductory course in voice and speech for effective communication. Exercises and practical applications in a variety of speaking contexts focus on vocal function, breath, resonance, articulation and coping with performance stress.

title: Production Practicum
description: Provides students with the opportunity to learn and practice the technical and management skills associated with creating a production. Required of all second-year students working in production and design. Open to majors/minors. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Theatre Department. Corequisite: FA/THEA 2110 6.00.

title: Production Practicum
description: Provides second-year production students with the opportunity to expand their learning and practice of technical and management skills associated with creating a production. Taken in conjunction with FA/THEA 2100 3.00 this course is open to second-year students working in production and design who want to work on more than one project in their second-year. Open to majors/minors. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Theatre Department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 2110 6.00.

title: Production Practicum
description: Provides second year production students with the opportunity to expand their learning and practice of technical and management skills associated with creating a production. An alternative to 2100 3.0 for all second-year students working in production and design who want to work on more than one project in their second year Open to majors/minors. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Theatre Department. Corequisite: FA/THEA 2110 6.00, FA/THEA 2410 6.

title: Production Practicum
description: Provides second year production students with the opportunity to expand their learning and practice of technical and management skills associated with creating a production. An alternative to 2100 3.0 for all second-year students working in production and design who want to work on more than one project in their second year Open to majors/minors. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Theatre Department. Corequisite: FA/THEA 2110 6.00, FA/THEA 2410 6.

title: 2nd year Stagecraft
description: Offers further practical exploration into the elements of theatrical production. Students will explore management, scenic, drafting, lighting and sound techniques. Required of all second-year students working in production and design. Open to theatre majors/minors or permission of the department. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 with a minimum grade of C+, FA/THEA 1200 6.00 and permission of the Department.

title: Introduction to Costuming for Performance
description: Introduction to Costuming for Performance equips the student with a comprehensive understanding of the varied disciplines required in the costume realization process. It examines techniques from conception to final costume fabrication and how costumes are integral to performance. The course focuses on the practical skills needed for managing a costume shop, pattern drafting, costume construction, and maintenance. By learning the proper use of the equipment and employing costuming techniques, students will be well-prepared to continue their work in this field. Open to majors and non-majors. Studio Course meets 6 hours a week for the fall term.

title: Introduction to Costuming for Performance 2
description: Introduction to Costuming for Performance 2 continues the work begun in FA/THEA 2120 3.00, further exploring the costuming process and equipping the student with a comprehensive understanding of the varied disciplines required in the costume realization process. It examines techniques from conception to final costume fabrication and how costumes are integral to performance. The course focuses on the practical skills needed for managing a costume shop and the crafts of costume construction. By learning the proper use of the equipment and employing costuming techniques, students will be well-prepared to continue their work in this field. Open to majors and non-majors. Studio Course meets 6 hours a week for the winter term.

title: Introduction to Sculpture: Soft Sculpture
description: This Experiential Education course is designed to engage students in creating three-dimensional, non-wearable sculpture in soft materials such as textiles, flexible foam and paper. Through a combination of presentations and hands-on studio projects, this course will explore soft materials as a sculptural medium, and contextualize the use of soft materials in both historical and contemporary frameworks of artistic production, emphasizing individual, process-based approaches to creative problem solving. The sculptural processes surrounding fabrication of soft sculptures introduces students to a range of sculptural methodologies and skills employing pattern drafting, assembly, and material manipulation. Through in-class demonstrations students are introduced to a range of skills and tools to be utilized in the production of their studio projects. Assignments consist of a series of projects exploring different working processes and sculptural methodologies. In addition to these projects, in-class discussions, technical assignments and readings engage students in the dialogue surrounding contemporary sculptural concerns such as form, process and spatial awareness. Craftsmanship and a demonstrated knowledge of materials are a major factor in this course. In order for students to be able to fully articulate their idea in a given material, they must understand the limits and possibilities inherent in the fabrication process. It is expected that each student will develop a degree of sophistication and competence when working with these material processes. Lectures, demonstrations, group critiques and hands-on instruction are the essential means by which we will investigate sculptural problem-solving. The class participates in material specific demonstrations, technical assignments and class critiques of finished work. Periodically there will be in-class work periods, but it is expected that the majority of the assignments will be completed outside of class time.

title: Introduction to Design for Performance I
description: This class is an introduction to how theatrical design areas (which include set, costumes, light, sound, and projection) relate to storytelling and enhance an audience's connection and experience of the play. This form of non-verbal communication provides a mirror to our own cultural perspectives: how and why we see and experience the things we do when reading a script or translating the text into production. The course will examine different ways a designer approaches and deconstructs a theme in a script through references and research and how that translates to a final design. The elements and principles of design will be introduced and applied to assignments. These foundational design tools are transferable to many performance and entertainment disciplines, such as screen, dance, and musical performance. The course will include visiting guest speakers and may include off-campus site visits to view live performances. Open to majors and non-majors. Course Type: Studio delivery 3hs synchronous in studio, 3hs asynchronous per week for 12 weeks

title: History of Theatre and Performance
description: Offers an historical survey of theatre and performance from classical Athens to late C20. It examines theatre and performance in the larger social, cultural and political contexts by integrating critical analysis with explorations of various performance possibilities. Required of all second-year majors. Open to non-majors. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 and FA/THEA 1200 6.00 or permission of the Instructor.

title: Theatre and Social Justice
description: Provides a basis for continuing work in theatre studies. This course examines questions about the nature of theatre and its role in society. Required of all second-year theatre studies students. Open to non-majors. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 and FA/THEA 1200 6.00 or permission of the Instructor. Corequisite: For theatre majors, FA/THEA 2200 6.00.

title: Visual History for Stage and Screen
description: Charts a survey course through a visual history of human civilization's architecture, clothing, interior design, and furnishings, from the beginnings of civilization to the present day. There is a strong focus on honing research skills of primary visual sources. This course is a foundation for set, costume, and lighting designers of all types of live performance and media. We must know the rules before we can break them. Required of all theatre production students.

title: Time-Based Art: Crossing Boundaries
description: Introduces students to interdisciplinary studio practice, emphasizing critical thinking and creative exploration of time and process. Sound, video and performance are investigated. Technical workshops include introductions to sound and video editing, audio recorder and microphone use. This course is cross-listed between the Department of Visual Arts and the Theatre Department.

title: Time-Based Art: Performance Art and Everyday Life
description: Focuses on individual and group projects plus readings on time-based media, especially contemporary performance art. Students participate in exercises that promote original responses to the everyday environment, and are encouraged to use a variety of media in making works. This course is cross-listed between the Department of Visual Arts and the Theatre Department.

meetings.catNumber: B44T01 (FA VISA) X33S01 (FA THEA) B80E01 (FA DATT)

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides an intermediate practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre or organization. Prerequisite: Permission of the Theatre Department. Open to theatre majors and minors only.

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides an intermediate practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre/organization. Prerequisite: Permission of the Theatre Department. Open to theatre majors and minors only.

title: Voice: Classical Text & Intelligibility
description: A continuation of voice, speech, and text training principles and methodologies, including an examination of Canadian & American speech patterns and intelligibility for the stage. Exploration of Shakespeare text and Elizabethan rhetoric is used to research, personalize, and embody the dense meaning of complex language. Prerequisites: grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2010 3.00, or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Voice: Speech & Dialect
description: A continuation of voice, speech, and text training principles and methodologies, including an examination of the sounds of the world's languages, and the use of phonetics for the actor to describe those sounds. An exploration of accents of English is used to develop speech skills for transformational acting through the application to appropriate texts. Prerequisites: grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2010 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Acting: The Modern and Shakespearean Canons
description: Continued exploration of acting techniques, character development and play/text analysis begun in FA/THEA 2021 3.00, and a contemporary examination of theatrical canons that have influenced the development of Canadian Theatre. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2021 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Acting: The Play
description: FA/THEA 3021 continues the application and deepening of acting techniques, approaches to character development and text/play analysis through the in-class staging of a full play text. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 3020 3.00 or permission of the department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 3011 3.00 and FA/THEA 3031 3.00. Open to majors only.

title: Movement: Physical Range, Character Body, & Transformation
description: This intermediate level course is a continuation of techniques, principles and explorations of movement for the actor 2030. The course will help free up the body to play physically dynamic and varied characters and generally increase the students physical range for acting, using play, body language principles and mimicry. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2030 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Movement: Emotional Authenticity-Body, Voice & Acting
description: This course focuses on physical approaches to acting that include vocal work to increase emotional range and authenticity. The class integrates rigorous vocal and physical training that teaches the student to use physical awareness to access emotional expression necessary for acting. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2030 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Introduction to Clown and Mask for Performers
description: Designed to introduce the principles of dynamic whole-body performance through play and improvisation based in mask and clown work. A variety of clown styles and techniques will be studied, such as stage clown, Pochinko clown, bouffon and baby clown. The course will also cover an introduction to neutral mask, as well as character mask. A simple mask will be made in class. This class will assist the actor to find freedom and the courage to go beyond naturalism, with authenticity and spontaneity. By assisting the performer to free up their impulses, students will build new and varied characters and find a playful approach to acting in general. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA2021 3.00 or FA/THEA 2051 3.00, and FA/THEA2030 and FA/THEA2010, and/or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: An Introduction to Motion Capture Performance for Actors
description: Introduces the performer to the world of motion capture (mocap), using both practical and creative approaches. Utilizing their previous Actor training, students will learn: to perform in a digital environment; the importance of creating fully-realized scenes using only their imagination and a script; to live and play in imagined worlds using few (or no) props, set pieces, or costumes; and the requisite technical requirements for mocap performance, many of which are uncommon to other acting genres. Students work on scenes from professional AAA video games and will be encouraged to heighten character stakes and rediscover the freedom to play, while keeping their work authentic and organic. Collaboration and constructive feedback from peers is expected, and crucial to developing an understanding of this craft. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2021 or FA/THEA 2051, and FA/THEA 2030 and FA/THEA 2010, and/or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Devised Theatre in Practice I
description: Rigorously develops the processes and skills of devising and interpreting theatre works within a collaborative context. In classroom exercises, and through the rehearsal and performance of assigned performance projects, students will explore and practice the creative approaches of the theatre practitioner. Practical studio course. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2051 3.00, and permission of the department. Open to majors only. Note: Plus rehearsal hours. Corequisite: FA/THEA 3200 3.00.

title: Devised Theatre in Practice II
description: Building on the processes and skills investigated in FA/THEA 3050 3.00, this practical studio course offers students further opportunities to practice the creation and presentation of devised theatre pieces in a collaborative setting. Classroom exercises and assigned performance projects will prepare participants for their final year public showcase in FA/THEA 4050 3.00 and FA/THEA 4051 3.00. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 3050 3.00 and permission of the Theatre Department. Open to majors only. Note: Plus rehearsal hours.

title: Public Speaking:Prep,Practice,Present
description: Examines how to prepare and practice for presentations in seminars, office, public events. Develops physical, vocal and rhetorical skills needed for public presentations. Prerequisite: third- or fourth- year standing, FA/THEA 2060.3.00 or permission of the department. Open to theatre majors and non-majors.

title: Performance Practicum I
description: Intended for third-year students working in acting, or in assistant directing mounted or unmounted department productions in the fall term. This course offers an intensive opportunity to develop and improve skills in the creation of workshop productions. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 2021 3.00 or FA/THEA 2051 3.00 and/or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Performance Practicum II
description: Intended for third-year students in acting, or in assistant directing mounted or unmounted department productions in the winter term. This course offers an intensive opportunity to develop and improve skills in the creation of workshop productions. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 3020 3.00 or FA/THEA 3050 3.00 and/or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Production Practicum
description: Required of all third-year students working in production and design. The course gives students an opportunity to experience all aspects of creating a show (including stage management) from a production standpoint. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 2100 or FA/THEA 2101 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Production/Design Area. Corequisite: At least one other studio course in theatre production. Note: Students may take FA/THEA 3100 3.00 or FA/THEA 3101 6.00, but not both concurrently. Open to majors and minors only or by permission of the department.

Prerequisites: FA/THEA 2100 or FA/THEA 2101 or FA/THEA 2103/6/9 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Production/Design Area. Corequisite: At least one other studio course in theatre production. Note: Students may take FA/THEA 3100 3.00 or FA/THEA 3106 6.00, but not both concurrently. Note: Open to majors and minors only or by permission of the department.

Corequisite: At least one other studio course in theatre production. Students may take FA/THEA 3100 3.00 or FA/THEA 3106 6.00, but not both concurrently. Open to majors and minors only or by permission of the department.

The course gives students an opportunity to experience all aspects of creating a show (including stage management) from a production standpoint. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 2100 or FA/THEA 2101 or FA/THEA 2103/6/9 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Production/Design Area. Corequisite: At least one other studio course in theatre production. Note: Students may take FA/THEA 3100 or FA/THEA 3109, but not both concurrently. Open to majors and minors only or by permission of the department.

title: Props and Paint for Performance and Cosplay
description: Explores the principles and practice of producing properties and scenic art for performance and Cosplay. Course credit exclusion: FA/THEA 3171 3.00. Studio course meets 3 hours a week for the year.

title: Costuming for Performance
description: This course is designed to provide an intensive application and further development of work begun in FA/THEA 2120 3.00. The course's primary focus is on the exciting and practical skills of costume drafting, construction, and the proper use of equipment and costume materials for theatre, dance, screen, and cosplay. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 2120 3.00 or permission from Department of Theatre, Dance and Performance. Studio Course that meets 3 hours a week for the full year.

title: Technology in Arts Management
description: Trains students to use current technologies to mange both production and their own careers. Students will be introduced to the fundamental concepts and uses of many computer programs and protocols that will be helpful for furthering themselves in their professions. Students will learn the basic skills needed to establish a web presence for information distribution and self promotion, familiarize themselves with best practices and operation of databases to better manage and record information, and work with common graphic design and presentation software to create more effective and clear documentation.

title: Scenic Drafting for Stage and Screen
description: This blended lecture and online course familiarizes students with technical drawing for the stage and screen for a technician and designer alike. This involves the ability not only to communicate technical material for a design's realization, but also to translate renderings and/or models into technical drawings for costing and construction. This course is suitable for both students of stage scenography and screen based media production. Course type: Studio hybrid on-line 3hrs/week for 12 weeks

title: Design for Performance II
description: This class builds on foundational knowledge from Introduction to Design for Performance I (THEA2141). Focused on set, costume, lighting, sound, and media design, this course will guide students through the design process, including introduction and development of skills like script review and breakdowns, drafting, model building, renderings, and industry-standard paperwork. Students will be pushed to think outside the box and to challenge audiences' perceptions, and how to communicate design ideas with clarity. Students will have the option to focus their studies in specific design disciplines and make full use of our design studio, lighting lab, the Makerspace, carpentry and costume shops. This course is intended to give students the foundations of design theory, skills, and professional best practices to prepare them as they move into THEA3147 Design for Performance III. Excursions to professional productions and special guest speakers will bring the industry to our classroom. Prerequisites: FA/THEA2110 2nd Year Stagecraft, FA/THEA2141 Introduction to Design for Performance I, and FA/THEA2410 Visual History for Stage & Screen. Co-Requisites: Set designers require FA/THEA 3142 3.0 Drawing for the Theatre and FA/THEA 3145 3.0 Technical Drawing for Theatre. Costume designers require FA/THEA 2120 3.0 Introduction to Costuming for Performance and FA/THEA 3142 3.0 Drawing for the Theatre. Lighting & Media designers require FA/THEA 3145 3.0 Technical Drawing for Theatre. Or by permission of the Theatre Department. Open to non-majors? (Y/N): Y

title: Design for Performance III
description: This class builds on foundational knowledge from Design for Performance II (THEA3146). The purpose of the course is to lead the student through various phases of analysis, research, and the creative process required for design disciplines for live performance. The design process will be comprehensively examined through the framework of preparation, exploration, collaboration and execution of a complete design. Students will have studio time to explore projects and may also be able to learn from a variety of special guest speakers that range from directors to other designers and trades. We will also cover different styles of performance such as screen and exploring the elements and principals of design are transferable to different performance mediums. Course will include visiting guest speakers and may include trips to theatres. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 3143 3.0 Set & Costume Design for Performance II OR THEA 3146 3.0 Design for Performance II, and FA/THEA 3145 3.0 Technical Drawing for Theatre. Open to non-majors? (Y/N): Y

title: Theatre Management
description: Introduces students to the principles of theatre management and organization including staffing, budgeting, fund raising, box office and production management. Note: This course or FA/THEA 4150 3.00 is required of all majors. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 2200 6.00. Corequisite: Non-majors by permission of the Instructor.

title: Stage Management
description: A full year course with in-person and asynchronous seminars and labs in the fall term and a focus on practical experiential learning in the winter term. The course is practicum in the art of stage management, consisting of lectures and seminars on theory, methodology and organization. Focused is on practical application and development of skills. Fall term will be classroom and studio focused meeting weekly during the scheduled class time. The winter term will focus on practical skills though experiential learning opportunities like community-focused learning opportunities, and work-focused practicums. There be limited in-person meetings during the scheduled class time. Students are expected to work outside of class time on shows, events, films, and/or job shadows and report and reflect on their experiences. (40-50 hours). Travel off campus may be required. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 2106 6.00 or permission of the Department.

title: Screen Acting: Practical Approaches to the Craft of the Actor
description: Offers an introduction to the complexities of the actor's process as it relates to contemporary film and television production. This course is open to all Arts, Media, Performance & Design students and theatre majors.

title: Intro to Playwriting
description: Through readings of both published and student-written material, in-class discussions and foundational dramaturgical skills, students work towards creation and development of theatrical writing. Emphasizing skills development, this process-oriented course builds on discoveries made through performance and how it is applied to a script. Prerequisites: Submission of portfolio and permission of Instructor.

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides An advanced practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre. Prerequisite: Permission of the production area, by special arrangement. Open only to theatre majors.

title: Independent Production Practicum
description: Provides An advanced practicum in production technique usually based on training and experience with a professional theatre. Prerequisite: Permission of the production area, by special arrangement. Open only to theatre majors.

title: Voice: Accent & Voice-Over
description: A continuation of voice, speech, and text training principles and methodologies, including an examination of different vocal levels for stage, screen and voice-over. Further exploration of accents, and the introduction of on-mic technique for a range of voice-over styles. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 2010 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Acting: Audition & Showcase Preparation
description: Acting: Audition and Showcase Preparation offers students an in-depth exploration of the tools needed for the selection, analysis, rehearsal, and performance of monologues, an essential career skill for the professional actor. Acting techniques will build on and further develop the work begun in the second and third years of the Acting program and will culminate in presenting material for Next Generation Showcase in Toronto. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 3021 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Acting for Camera
description: Acting for Camera offers students an in-depth exploration of the tools needed to act in film and television, in addition to essential career skills for professional actors. Students will rehearse and present a variety of scenes for the camera, deepen their understanding of the acting process and auditioning through on-camera analysis, and develop skills to promote themselves in audition circumstances. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 4020 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Movement: Physical Performance Skills
description: This movement course focuses on physical theatre creation. This class offers training in various approaches to physical improvisation as a tool to create theatre; both to devise compelling characters for scripted work as well as create your own performance material. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 3030 3.00 or FA/THEA 3031 3.00 or permission of the department. Open to majors only.

title: Performance Styles of Acting
description: This course introduces the performer to acting approaches for a variety of styles of Theatre. In tandem with the Performance Creation (PC) program, Acting & Performance students will focus on two styles of theatre, to further broaden their range of methods when working on both text and non-text-based performances. Styles to be studied may include, but are not limited to: Comedy, Musical Theatre, Feminist Theatre, Indigenous Theatre, Cultural Styles (such as Butoh), as well as Period Styles (such as Restoration, Melodrama, Ancient Greek or Roman Theatre). The styles will be chosen in tandem with the Performance Creation curriculum and the instructors' skillsets from year to year. This course will culminate in presentations of scenes from the students' work in each style for peers and a limited audience, to provide students with valuable feedback from the live nature of this craft. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in THEA 3021 3.0 or THEA 3051 3.0 or permission of the department.

title: Devised Theatre Perspectives
description: Offers students in their final year of Devised Theatre an intensive curriculum in further perspectives of devised theatre exploration. Incorporating skill sets from the previous two years of training, this class will focus on advanced techniques for creating and performing original theatre works in a group setting, in preparation for a performance in the Devised Theatre Festival in the winter term. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in FA/THEA 3051 3.00 and permission of the Theatre Department. Open to majors only. Note: Plus rehearsal hours.

title: Devised Theatre Workshop
description: Offers an opportunity for students to consolidate their training by creating and performing their own piece(s) for a public performance in the Devised Theatre Festival at the end of the winter term. In accordance with the self-reliant nature of this series of classes, students will participate fully in all aspects of the collaborative devising of theatre in these presentations, from conception to execution, with minimal dependence on external technical support. Prerequisites: Minimum of B in FA/THEA 4050 3.00 and permission of the Theatre Department. Open to majors only. Note: Plus rehearsal hours.

title: Performance Practicum III
description: Intended for final-year students in acting, or in assistant directing mounted department productions in the fall term. This course gives students an intensive opportunity to develop advanced skills in the creation of a fully mounted production. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 3021 3.00 or FA/THEA 3050 3.00, and/or permission of the Theatre Department. For assistant directors, it is recommended to take FA/THEA 4485 3.00. Open to Theatre majors only.

title: Performance Practicum IV
description: Intended for final-year students in acting, or in assistant directing mounted department productions in the winter term. This course gives students an intensive opportunity to develop advanced skills in the creation of a fully mounted production. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 4020 3.00 or FA/THEA 4050 3.00, and/or permission of the Theatre Department. Corequisites for Specialized Honours BFA Program (Acting) FA/THEA 4011 3.00 and FA/THEA 4021 3.00. For assistant directors, it is recommended to take FA/THEA 4485 3.00. Open to Theatre majors only.

title: Production Practicum II
description: Required of all fourth-year students working in production and design, the course gives advanced students an opportunity to further develop and perfect skills in the creation of a show. Labs include work on departmental productions. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 3100 3.00 or FA/THEA 3101 6.00 with a minimum grade of C+ or by permission of the Production/Design Area. Corequisite: At least one other 4000-level course in theatre production. Open to non-majors by permission of the department. Note: Students may take FA/THEA 4100 3.00 or FA/THEA4101 6.00, but not both concurrently.

title: Production Practicum II
description: Required of all fourth-year students working in production and design, the course gives advanced students an opportunity to further develop and perfect skills in the creation of a show. Labs include work on departmental productions. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 3100 3.00 or FA/THEA 3101 3.00 or 6.00 or FA/THEA 3103 3.0 or FA/THEA 3106 6.0.

title: Production Practicum II
description: Required of all fourth-year students working in production and design, the course gives advanced students an opportunity to further develop and perfect skills in the creation of a show. Labs include work on departmental productions. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 3100 3.0 or FA/THEA 3101 6.0 or FA/THEA 3106 6.0.

title: Production Practicum II
description: Required of all fourth-year students working in production and design, the course gives advanced students an opportunity to further develop and perfect skills in the creation of a show. Labs include work on departmental productions. Prerequisite: FA/THEA 3100 or FA/THEA 3101 or FA/THEA 3103, 3106, or 3109.

title: Eco-Scenography Studio
description: In the eco-scenographic studio, we approach the design of performance projects from an ecological, systems thinking approach in an expanded context. This course explores a range of scenarios that problematize conventional theatrical presentations, including remote site-specific production; applied, socially engaged, and community-based work; in-tegration of renewable energy and sustainable materials; collaboration with indigenous partners; and projects with both human and non-human performers. In the course students, will examine a variety of case study productions and approach their design, or elements of their design, from eco-scenography. These case-studies will be contextual-ized by current research in the field. Students will engage in theoretical and practical design projects guide by their study with experiential op-portunities on- and off-campus. Open to non-majors.

title: Design for Performance IV
description: This advanced theatrical set, costume, lighting, sound, and video design course will focus on further honing technical design skills and learning to communicate with directors and technicians to understand how to realize designs. At this point students should be well versed in the elements and principles of design and how to use those to create strong conceptual design ideas inspired by text/script and how to navigate the design process. Students may have the opportunity to collaborate with a student director to conceive and execute a design from the beginning of the process to the first day of rehearsal. Course will include visiting guest speakers and trips to live performance. Prerequisites: FA/THEA2141 Introduction to Design for Performance I. Open to Theatre majors, minors and non-majors. Enrolment by application and permission of the course director. Open to non-majors? (Y/N): Y

title: Perspectives on Contemporary Theatre
description: Explores some of the innovative and challenging developments in dramatic writing and theatrical performance in the last 25 years, in Canada and internationally. Prerequisites: For theatre majors, FA/THEA 3200 3.00.

title: Popular Theatre & Performance - From Circus to Drag and Beyond
description: Investigates the history, structure, and style of popular nineteenth-century performance genres including but not limited to vaudeville, burlesque, circuses, and freak shows, as well as more recent ""genres"" including but not limited to bodybuilding, hip hop dancing, and fashion shows. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 1010 3.00, FA/THEA 1100 3.00 and FA/THEA 1200 6.00; FA/THEA 2210, FA/THEA 2200 or permission of the Instructor. Open to Non-Majors.

title: Independent Study I
description: For highly motivated fourth-year Theatre majors who have an Overall GPA of 6.0 or better and a Major GPA of 7.0 or better, and who wish to pursue special and intensive personal study in an independent non-studio course under the supervision of an appropriate Area faculty member. Note: Open by application to the Department of Theatre Undergraduate Education Committee.

title: Independent Study I
description: For highly motivated fourth-year Theatre majors who have an Overall GPA of 6.0 or better and a Major GPA of 7.0 or better, and who wish to pursue special and intensive personal study in an independent non-studio course under the supervision of an appropriate Area faculty member. Note: Open by application to the Department of Theatre Undergraduate Education Committee.

title: Independent Study II
description: For highly motivated fourth-year Theatre majors who have an Overall GPA of 6.0 or better and a Major GPA of 7.0 or better, and who wish to pursue special and intensive personal study in an independent studio course under the supervision of an appropriate Area faculty member. Note: Open by application to the Department of Theatre Undergraduate Education Committee.

title: Independent Study II
description: For highly motivated fourth-year Theatre majors who have an Overall GPA of 6.0 or better and a Major GPA of 7.0 or better, and who wish to pursue special and intensive personal study in an independent studio course under the supervision of an appropriate Area faculty member. Note: Open by application to the Department of Theatre Undergraduate Education Committee.

title: The Theatricality Of Power:  Violence, memory, and revolution
description: Examines the use of theatre, spectacle, and theatricality- by the state, by oppositional groups, and by performance practitioners - to establish or challenge structures of power. Prerequisite: 3000-level standing or permission of the Instructor. PRIOR TO WINTER 2017: course Credit Exclusion: FA/FACS 3100 3.00.

title: Aspects of Directing
description: Provides an Investigation and application of the fundamental and intermediate principles of directing for the theatre. Prerequisites: FA/THEA 3051 3.00 or FA/THEA 3210 6.00 or FA/THEA 3290 6.00; FA/THEA 3070 3.00 or FA/THEA 3071 3.00; or by application to the department. Corequisites: FA/THEA 4070 3.00 or FA/THEA 4071 3.00. Course credit exclusion: FA/THEA 4480 6.00.

title: Graduate One Directing
description: N/A

title: Solo Performance Creation; Devising for Solo Performance in any Medium
description: Through sourcing exercises, presentations of student-created material, and feedback, students develop material for solo performance in any medium. The class focuses on creation rather than production. Prerequisites: Some studio training required (dance, digital media, acting). Submission of a resume (portfolio/video if available), interest statement and permission of Instructor. Available to MFA students in theatre and MA/PhD students in Theatre and Performance Studies.

title: EcoScenography Studio
description: In Eco-scenography studio, we approach the design of performance projects from an ecological, systems-thinking approach. This course explores a range of scenarios that problematize conventional theatrical presentations including remote site-specific production; applied, socially engaged, and community-based work; integration of renewable energy and sustainable materials; collaboration with indigenous partners; and projects with human and non-human performers.

title: Historical Sources for Designs and Directors
description: This is a survey course relating the architecture, art, clothing, interior design and furnishings of world civilization to the theatre. The course also touches on the visual aspects of the theatrical styles of various periods. Required of all design and directing students.

title: Graduate One Ecological Design for the Performing Arts
description: Provides the opportunity to work on complex projects through the various areas of theatrical design in traditional theatre, dance or opera incorporating sustainability in space, design and production methods. Corequisites: GS/THEA 5210 3.00, GS/THEA 5410 3.00, GS/THEA 5412 3.00

title: Theatre Laboratory
description: This course will examine methods for transforming research into performance practice and for using performance practice as a laboratory for conducting research. Bridging the assumed divide between practice and theory, students will create performances that explore the central questions engaged by their research projects.

title: Theatre, Dance, & Performance Studies Placement
description: This course is designed to give graduate students applied, professionally-oriented work experience in a field related to one of the program's fields of specialization and/or the student's research areas. Note: This course is graded on a pass/fail basis.

title: Theatre, Dance and Performance Studies Graduate Colloquium
description: This course discusses research approaches, pedagogical strategies, and various aspects of professional development within theatre and performance studies. This course is required for and only open to Theatre, Dance & Performance Studies MA students and first-year PhD students.

title: Popular Theatre, Dance, & Performance - From Circus to Drag and Beyond
description: Investigates the histories, dramaturgies, embodied practices, and ideological underpinnings of popular nineteenth-century performance genres and traces their lingering influences on twenty-first century entertainment.

title: Independent Studies
description: This course is an opportunity for advanced research and in-depth reading in advanced aspects of theatre studies including but not limited to postcolonial theatre and drama, theory and performance studies and theatre, health and social change.

title: Teaching and Learning Seminar
description: The purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of the current pedagogy, practices and policy relating to the teaching of Deaf and Hard-of -Hearing students. The course content provides a framework for understanding the instructional techniques encountered in practicum placements. The practicum component of this course exposes teachers candidates to the range of educational environments as well as the communication philosophies and modalities used in the education of Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing students. NOTE: Courses in this program are part of a professional post-graduate diploma program, and are not open for registration to students outside the program. Courses are not open for auditing.

title: Practicum 1
description: Teacher candidates participate in one practicum experience over the course of the academic year. NOTE: Courses in this program are part of a professional post-graduate diploma program, and are not open for registration to students outside the program. Courses are not open for auditing.

title: Practicum 2
description: Teacher candidates participate in one practicum experience over the course of the academic year. NOTE: Courses in this program are part of a professional post-graduate diploma program, and are not open for registration to students outside the program. Courses are not open for auditing.

title: Teaching Deaf and Hard of Hearing Learners in Inclusive Settings
description: The purpose of this course is to provide candidates with the skills and knowledge needed to plan, implement, and assess education plans for Deaf and Hard of Hearing learners in inclusive settings. Candidates will critically examine the social and emotional needs of D/HH learners in inclusive settings and discuss strategies and methods used to enable D/HH learners to be socially included with their peers in the classroom setting. NOTE: Courses in this program are part of a professional post-graduate diploma program, and are not open for registration to students outside the program. Courses are not open for auditing.

title: Translation and Mobility
description: Le séminaire vise à mieux comprendre linscription de la traduction dans un environnement multilingue et multiethnique, ainsi que dans les enjeux de la mondialisation. Seront abordées en particulier les questions du brouillage des frontières et du positionnement identitaire.

title: Comparative and World Literature Seminar: History and Practice
description: Introduces students to the conditions of emergence and development of the discipline of Comparative Literature from its beginnings in nineteenth-century Europe to its most recent global iteration of World Literature. Students will experience how expanded understandings of cultural translation and textuality have radically altered and expanded the Eurocentric character of the discipline. Questions for investigation includes: How have the aesthetics and politics of Comparative Literature changed over the past two hundred years? What factors have influenced those changes? How is World Literature related to Comparative Literature? How do both relate to colonial, post-colonial, diasporic, cultural and translation studies and digital humanities?

title: Mechatronics System Design and Implementation I
description: This course is an introductory course in mechatronics. It introduces the topic through both in-class material and a laboratory-based component within which students participate in two team-based mini-projects. The course provides an overview of the subject area through specific case studies drawn from existing commercial systems, and uses two mini- projects to highlight mechatronics processes and technologies. The laboratory is also used to provide basic health and safety training, as well as hands-on training on specific electrical, electronic and mechanical technologies. Pre-requisites: Open to students enrolled in a BEng degree program.

title: Mechatronics System Design and Implementation II
description: This course is an intermediate course in mechatronics. Building upon TRON 1000, the course develops uses the development of more advanced mechatronics system to introduce more complex electronics, sensing, control and mechanical vibration, and actuation principles. The laboratory provides basic health and safety training, as well as hands-on training on specific electrical, electronic, mechanical vibrations and mechanical technologies. Teamwork and team leadership is introduced through mentorship and review of TRON 1000 projects. Pre-requisites: LE/TRON 1000 3.00 or LE/EECS 1028 3.00 or LE/ESSE 1012 3.00.

title: Corporate Taxation I - Overview and Private Corporations
description: This course is a survey of the tax policy issues and laws relating to the taxation of corporations and their shareholders. It is designed for students with little background in the Canadian rules for taxing corporations and shareholders.

title: Overview of United States Taxation and Recent Developments
description: N/A

title: International Taxation I: Policy and System Design
description: International taxation topics covered in this course include: jurisdiction to tax; the foreign affiliate system; foreign tax credit; corporate immigration; emigration and continuance, aspects of transfer pricing; ownership and financing of overseas operations of Canadian companies; structuring foreign joint ventures, financing US affiliates, cross-border mergers and de-mergers and other forms of corporate reorganizations; alternative inbound investment structures; international finance companies, computer software; cross-border issues; and issues relating to tax treaties.

title: Partnerships and Tax Shelters
description: N/A

title: Tax Planning and Avoidance
description: Taxing statutes and tax planning are closely linked: new and amended tax measures result in practitioners using new strategies to reduce tax, and legislative steps to close gaps typically lead to further, responsive approaches by tax advisors. This course delves into fundamental concepts that engage with the 'strange loop' of avoidance strategies and legislative and judicial anti-avoidance rules. Concepts discussed include the form-over-substance doctrine, sham and window-dressing, statutory interpretation, structural elements of specific anti-avoidance rules and the general anti-avoidance rule.

title: Planning Suburbs
description: From garden suburbs to post-war inner- and outer-suburbs, from New Urbanist communities to edge cities, technoburbs, and exurbs, this course critically considers the planning of suburban built form and the suburbanization process in historical perspective. Consideration is given to the mechanisms and the challenges of managing suburban growth, and to the complex socio-cultural geographies and values that shape the suburbs and the suburban way of life. Attention is directed to issues of gender, racialized poverty, unemployment, infrastructural inadequacy, sprawl, and sustainability, and an effort is made to envision alternative futures.

title: Teaching Visual Arts in the Intermediate Division
description: This course begins to prepare students to be qualified teachers of Visual Arts in Ontario classrooms. It allows students to examine the theories, philosophies, knowledge, policies and practices specific to teaching visual arts in the intermediate and senior grades. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (BEd) degree program.

title: Teaching Visual Arts in the Intermediate-Senior Division - A
description: This course begins to prepare students to be qualified teachers of Visual Arts in Ontario classrooms. It allows students to examine the theories, philosophies, knowledge, policies and practices specific to teaching Visual Arts in the intermediate and senior grades. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (BEd) degree program.

title: Teaching Visual Arts in the Intermediate-Senior Division - B
description: This course continues to prepare students to be qualified teachers of Visual Arts in Ontario classrooms. It develops students' expertise in the theories, philosophies, knowledge, policies and practices specific to teaching Visual Arts areas in order to further develop students' expertise for teaching this subject. ED/VISA 4000 (Part A) is a prerequisite for this course. This course is only available to students in the Bachelor of Education (BEd) degree program.

title: The Photographic Experience
description: This fully online course provides non-majors with an introduction to photographic concepts, theories and practices using personal Smartphone cameras. Students participate in online classes comprised of lectures, readings, personal reflections, artist examples, image analysis and photographic assignments. Basic photographic techniques, creative methods, concepts and contemporary modes of mobile image creation are explored. A Smartphone equipped with a camera is required. Students are required to attend live weekly tutorial sessions over Zoom. Students looking for more advanced camera skills using a DSLR or mirrorless camera should enroll in VISA 2061. This course cannot be used as a prerequisite for 3000 level photography courses. Open to non-majors only.

title: Art Fundamentals: Concept, Creativity and Production
description: Introduces students to the visual arts studios, faculty and a spectrum of production methods addressing two dimensional, three dimensional and the element of time in art making. An established theme provides students with a starting point for research, conceptualization and the exploration of fundamental processes as a means of visualizing their creative ideas. Course work is presented at an end of term exhibition.

title: Painting Approaches to the Human Figure
description: Examines Aesthetics and techniques through the study of various traditions and approaches to painting the human figure. Visual vocabulary and formal composition are developed through practical application and critical appraisal. Contemporary art concerns are discussed in slide presentations.

title: Painting: Composition and Colour
description: Introduces composition and colour through a number of assigned painting projects on how to structure a painting. Emphasis is on formal elements, particularly colour, and combining them through a diversity of compositional means that cover a range of painting genres. Course credit exclusion: FA/VISA 2022 3.00.

title: Painting: Approaches to Techniques and Materials
description: Explores a range of approaches to painting through a study of both traditional and contemporary techniques and materials. Students develop the technical and conceptual competency required for further exploration in painting, and discuss contemporary issues relating to the practice.

title: Introduction to Sculpture: Soft Sculpture
description: This Experiential Education course is designed to engage students in creating three-dimensional, non-wearable sculpture in soft materials such as textiles, flexible foam and paper. Through a combination of presentations and hands-on studio projects, this course will explore soft materials as a sculptural medium, and contextualize the use of soft materials in both historical and contemporary frameworks of artistic production, emphasizing individual, process-based approaches to creative problem solving. The sculptural processes surrounding fabrication of soft sculptures introduces students to a range of sculptural methodologies and skills employing pattern drafting, assembly, and material manipulation. Through in-class demonstrations students are introduced to a range of skills and tools to be utilized in the production of their studio projects. Assignments consist of a series of projects exploring different working processes and sculptural methodologies. In addition to these projects, in-class discussions, technical assignments and readings engage students in the dialogue surrounding contemporary sculptural concerns such as form, process and spatial awareness. Craftsmanship and a demonstrated knowledge of materials are a major factor in this course. In order for students to be able to fully articulate their idea in a given material, they must understand the limits and possibilities inherent in the fabrication process. It is expected that each student will develop a degree of sophistication and competence when working with these material processes. Lectures, demonstrations, group critiques and hands-on instruction are the essential means by which we will investigate sculptural problem-solving. The class participates in material specific demonstrations, technical assignments and class critiques of finished work. Periodically there will be in-class work periods, but it is expected that the majority of the assignments will be completed outside of class time.

title: Sculpture: Introductory Wood and Metal Fabrication
description: Engages students in three-dimensional, non-representational sculpture stressing individual approaches to creative problem solving. Introduces students to sculptural methodologies and skills employing additive and reductive processes. Discusses fundamental concepts of traditional, post-modern, and emerging sculptural production in relation to abstraction, as experienced through individual production. Mandatory safety equipment required.

title: Stone Carving
description: Develops understanding of form by combining primary sculptural method and traditional material. Investigations using stone identify principles of glyptic method and idea through dialogue, slide discussions and readings, resulting in visible signs of process and materialization of completed work. Compulsory supplementary fees. Mandatory safety equipment is required.

title: Introduction to Ceramic Sculpture
description: Designed to expose students to various processes used to develop sculpture in clay. Projects will focus on themes relevant to understanding object materiality, and offers a solid framework of clay and ceramic sculpture techniques, concept development, evaluation skills, and is the foundation for continuing on into Advanced Ceramic Sculpture.

title: Time-Based Art: Crossing Boundaries
description: Introduces students to interdisciplinary studio practice, emphasizing critical thinking and creative exploration of time and process. Sound, video and performance are investigated. Technical workshops include introductions to sound and video editing, audio recorder and microphone use. This course is cross-listed between the Department of Visual Arts and the Theatre Department.

title: Time-Based Art: Performance Art and Everyday Life
description: Focuses on individual and group projects plus readings on time-based media, especially contemporary performance art. Students participate in exercises that promote original responses to the everyday environment, and are encouraged to use a variety of media in making works. This course is cross-listed between the Department of Visual Arts and the Theatre Department.

title: Time-Based Art: Introduction to Video Art - Production
description: Introduces students to the creative practice of video art in a production studio environment, including both concepts and techniques. Classes include workshops on camera, lighting, video effects and sound recording techniques. Students create individual creative video projects. Compulsory supplementary fees.

title: Photography: The Black & White Darkroom
description: This hands-on studio course is an exploration of B&W processes and darkroom technique in a contemporary context. With a focus on analogue production, students are taught B&W negative and print production, DIY camera creation and camera-less photography techniques. Technical proficiency and aesthetic awareness are nurtured alongside the development of concept-driven artworks. This course has compulsory supplementary fees. Students are required to work on campus. Access to an analogue, manually operable camera is required. Students seeking camera and photography fundamentals should register in VISA 2061. VISA 2060 is open to visual arts majors.

title: Photography Fundamentals - Camera to Print
description: This course offers an introductory studio in photographic theory and practice fundamentals. Tools, techniques and ideas related to seeing and photo-based art are explored with emphasis on the photographer as an informed image-maker. Students gain hands-on skills in camera fundamentals, capture and printing, while developing an understanding of the basic principles of lens-based image making. Short, topic-oriented production assignments enable ongoing critical reflection and analysis. This course has compulsory supplementary fees. Access to a DSLR or mirrorless camera is mandatory and not available through VAAH. Students will require access to a computer equipped with Adobe Photoshop (on-campus computers are available in The Intersections Lab - ROOM 328). Students seeking photographic post-production techniques for the screen & web should register in VISA 2065. Open to visual arts majors and is a prerequisite for 3000-level photography courses.

title: Photography: Post Production for Screen & Web
description: This online course introduces students to photographic software and concepts related to the digital environment. Students will acquire skills in digital workflow and image processing by introducing raw files to Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop. Students will use software to produce and manipulate photographs for the screen & web. By the end of the course students will have acquired a working knowledge of the basic tools, applications and creative techniques related to digital, screen-based photography. This course has compulsory supplementary fees. Students will require access to a computer equipped with Adobe Lightroom Classic and Photoshop. Access to a DSLR camera is advantageous. Requires skill in basic digital photography. Students seeking camera and photography fundamentals should register in VISA 2061 before taking this course. VISA 2065 is open to visual arts majors and is a prerequisite for 3000-level photography courses. This course is cross-listed with FA/FILM 2065 3.00 and is open to Film majors (BA and BFA). Course credit exclusions: FA/VISA 2006 3.00; FA/FILM 2065 3.00.
